golden_baseline_location: $OTTERWORKS_LEGACY_ROOT/incoming/ and $OTTERWORKS_LEGACY_ROOT/archive/ from a deterministic legacy run of the unit's own namespace (make legacy-etl-gen-data NS=<ns> then TP_FAKETIME='2026-01-15 00:00:00' scripts/tp-run-deterministic.sh make legacy-etl-run JOB=sftp_ingest_poll NS=<ns>)

acceptance_checks.description: Every file the legacy poller moved into incoming/ is present in the landing volume for the namespace, same file names, same byte count per file (3430 bytes each for the two-file demo seed).
SHA-256 of each landed object equals the SHA-256 of the corresponding legacy incoming/ file — bytes are transported unmodified.

No partially-written file is ever visible to the downstream reader: landing is a single atomic publish (upload to a staging path then move, or Auto Loader commit), replacing the legacy size-compared-twice settle protocol.
No hostname-conditional behaviour anywhere in the converted job; one code path for all environments.
Concurrency is bounded by the platform (max_concurrent_runs=1 on the job), not by lock files that are never removed; a second concurrent trigger neither double-lands nor is blocked forever.
Re-running the ingest over the same source drop lands no duplicate rows/objects and leaves bronze row counts unchanged.
A run with an empty drop directory completes successfully, lands nothing, and leaves prior bronze output intact.

planted_anomalies.description: A file still being written when the poller fires must never be read downstream; the converted job must only publish complete objects.
The legacy 'parse lock exists, probably stale, proceeding' path must not exist: mutual exclusion is platform-enforced.

planted_anomalies.reason: Trailer/record-count reconciliation is the parse unit's responsibility (dbx-parse); the ingest unit is byte-transparent and does not interpret record content.

encoding_policy.input_encoding: none — treat CUSTBILL drops as opaque bytes (the legacy ksh/bash stages have no decoding layer)
encoding_policy.byte_transparency: required: bronze landing must preserve source bytes exactly; no decode/re-encode, no newline translation, no trimming
encoding_policy.invalid_bytes: must not fail the run; invalid byte sequences are landed as-is and only interpreted (and possibly quarantined) downstream in silver

malformed_record_policy.details: The ingest unit does not parse records, so it tolerates any content; it must never substitute a default or empty value for a missing source attribute (file name, size, source period) — a missing attribute fails the run rather than landing a plausible-looking row.

empty_input_semantics.details: Empty drop directory: succeed, land nothing, do not truncate or delete prior bronze output.
